clue.text: Writ served by journalist to writer-North American

parts.note: a sub, short for sub-editor, is a newspaper journalist
Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: A legal summons is delivered by a reporter to an American author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served by' and 'to' are link words; the hyphen just joins the writer to NA.
explanation.definitionFit: A subpoena is a court order, a written command to appear as a witness.

clue.text: Game people left in ship

indicators.note: in places the word for left inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Players are left aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' is not a contest: game people are willing, good-natured ones, called good sports.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport is someone who takes things in good part, game for anything.

clue.text: Chop or beef in advance

indicators.note: chop means cut up, so the letters of or beef are chopped and rearranged

explanation.surface: A choice between a chop or beef, ordered ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chop' looks like a cut of meat but rearranges OR BEEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier, ahead of time: done beforehand.

clue.text: Edna making an appearance in 1984?

explanation.surface: A woman named Edna turns up in a particular year.
explanation.walkthrough: 1984 is Orwell's novel, not the year; O'Brien is the Inner Party official who tortures Winston Smith.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna O'Brien was an Irish novelist, and O'Brien is the Party interrogator in Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Religious person, new curate, receiving one in church office

parts.note: a nun is a religious woman

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the rearranged letters hold the next piece
new signals that the letters of curate are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nun and a new curate take someone into a church office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CURATE into CATURE, which 'receiving' opens to take I.
explanation.definitionFit: A nunciature is the office or residence of a papal nuncio, an ambassador of the Holy See.

clue.text: Series about corporation bankruptcy

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the short form for series wraps the next piece

parts.note: corporation is old British slang for a pot belly, so a tum

explanation.surface: A run of events surrounding a big company ends in it going bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a company, but here it is the jocular British word for a paunch, TUM. STUMER is slang for a dud cheque or a failure; to come a stumer is to go broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumer is slang for financial failure: a worthless cheque, or coming a cropper and going bust.

clue.text: Exhaust American?

parts.note: read as a noun, exhaust is a car part, and this asks for its American name

explanation.surface: An order to wear out a person from the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' looks like a verb meaning tire, but it is the car's exhaust pipe, and the question asks its American English name.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call the rear end of a car's exhaust system by this name.

clue.text: Large assembly of zanies in Maryland

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: MD is the postal abbreviation of the US state Maryland

indicators.note: assembly means putting together, so the letters of zanies are assembled afresh

explanation.surface: A big gathering of clowns in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly of' rearranges ZANIES to ANSIZE, which goes inside MD.
explanation.definitionFit: Big enough for a grown man: generously proportioned.

clue.text: One visiting Derby?

parts.note: Derby is not the English city but the famous horse race at Epsom, so the visitor goes to the races

explanation.surface: Someone making a trip to the city of Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is a city in the English Midlands, but the Derby is also the great flat horse race run at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator at horse races attends meetings like the Derby.

clue.text: Biography less than nice about man in TV series

parts.note: bio is a short form of biography

indicators.note: less than a word means it falls short of its full length, so its final letter goes

explanation.surface: A life story that is not quite pleasant, about a television character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than nice' drops the last letter of NICE to give NIC. The definition recalls the 1970s TV shows The Six Million Dollar Man and The Bionic Woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The cyborg hero of the TV series The Bionic Man was given artificial body parts, the adjective describing him.

clue.text: Curry powder ingredient removed from cruet rim

indicators.note: removed signals that the letters of the following words are shifted out of their order

explanation.surface: Some spice has been taken off the edge of a condiment set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' reads as taking something away, but 'removed' rearranges the letters of CRUET RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmeric is the yellow spice that gives curry powder its colour.

clue.text: English parish priest in German forest

explanation.surface: An English clergyman finds himself in a forest in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German forest' reads as one phrase, but 'German' is just G and the forest is English: EPPING Forest lies on the north-east edge of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Epping Forest is an ancient woodland in Essex, on the edge of London.

clue.text: Soft material provides bubbles for masseur

parts.note: foam is a mass of bubbles
a masseur rubs people, so is a rubber

explanation.surface: Some soft stuff makes bubbles for a massage therapist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masseur' is read literally: one who rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A light spongy latex used for cushions and mattresses.

clue.text: Tense feeling which surrounds us?

explanation.surface: A strained mood that hangs all around people.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the mood of a place, tense or relaxed, and the layer of air enveloping the Earth.

clue.text: Wife's farewell after decline in Welsh community

indicators.note: after places the wife's farewell behind the decline piece

parts.note: to ebb is to decline, like the tide
W is the abbreviation for wife
vale is Latin for farewell

explanation.surface: A wife says goodbye after a slump in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: VALE is the Latin word for goodbye, used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebbw Vale is a former steel town in the South Wales valleys.

clue.text: Fresh planting soundly advised if lawn is this?

indicators.note: soundly signals that the words for fresh planting are taken by how they are said

parts.note: sowing seed afresh is reseeding

explanation.surface: Sowing again is wise advice for a thinning lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lawn' is hair on the head: a receding hairline might be advised to be reseeded, like a balding lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinning patch, like a hairline that is drawing back, shrinks as the edge retreats.

clue.text: Mark supports one embracing woman follower

indicators.note: in a down clue, supports means sits below, so the mark piece goes under one

parts.note: A is one, the indefinite article

parts.note: a dent is a mark
her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A man named Mark backs a person hugging a woman who follows a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a name but is a dent.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent sticks to a cause or leader: a supporter or disciple.

clue.text: Small change?

parts.note: read as slang, bread is money, so a small bit of bread is a little bit of money

explanation.surface: A question about loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, so the tiniest piece of it is a crumb of 'bread': small change.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny fragment of a loaf is a minute portion of bread, which is also slang for cash.

clue.text: Not in danger from mine exploding round Greek character

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the scrambled letters surround the Greek letter
exploding blows the letters of mine apart, into a new order

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is safe from a mine that blows up around a Greek man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploding' rearranges MINE to IMNE, which goes 'round' MU.
explanation.definitionFit: Being resistant or exempt means safe from a threat.

clue.text: Street artist has it depicted as a narrow stretch of water

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A street painter shows a channel in a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow channel joining two seas.

clue.text: This reflects radio waves, getting some delay eradicated

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A transmitter reflects signals, with some lag removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes the letters from inside dELAY ERadicated.

clue.text: Small person, one shedding tears

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
per. is an abbreviation for person in grammar

explanation.surface: A little person is crying.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cries, or a hired mourner at a funeral, sheds tears.

clue.text: Type of bronze girl is carrying hitherto not encountered

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the word for a girl wraps around the next piece

parts.note: gal is a colloquial word for a girl
something not met before is unmet

explanation.surface: A girl holds a bronze object she has never come across before.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunmetal is a bronze alloy of copper and tin once used to cast cannons.

clue.text: Article about extra pay cropped up

indicators.note: about means around, so the article is placed around the pay piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a rise is an increase in pay

explanation.surface: A news piece about a pay increase appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' is the grammar word, AN, not a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has arisen has come up or appeared, as an issue does.

clue.text: Foolishly buy card with nothing on, showing stubbornness

indicators.note: on means attached in front here, so the zero joins the rearranged letters

parts.note: O is the zero shape, nothing

indicators.note: foolishly suggests the letters of buy card are jumbled in a silly way

explanation.surface: Stubbornly buying a blank card is a silly act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolishly' rearranges BUY CARD to BDURACY, and O sits on it at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Obduracy is obstinate refusal to change one's mind, a showing of stubbornness.

clue.text: Height altering a fraction?

indicators.note: altering indicates that the letters of height change their order

explanation.surface: Changing a height by a small amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altering' rearranges HEIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: One part in eight is a fraction, written 1/8.

clue.text: Constable detaining others in rear, perhaps

indicators.note: detaining means holding within, so the rearranged letters wrap around the next piece
perhaps signals that the letters of rear are one possible arrangement, to be shuffled

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A police constable holds other people at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges REAR to ARER, which 'detaining' wraps around REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A police constable is someone whose job includes taking people into custody.
